newsitem.title: USA: Blue chip stocks end modestly higher.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip stocks end modestly higher.

text.p: Blue chips ended modestly higher Wednesday, supported by a rally in bonds and high-technology shares a day after the Federal Reserve surprised Wall Street by keeping interest rates unchanged.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 3.33 points at 5,877.36.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,298 to 1,033 on active volume of 451 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"Technology is doing well and bonds are doing very well. But there's still some caution. People are not rushing head-long into the market," said Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond rose 23/32, or $7.1875 per $1,000 face value, and its yield fell to 6.93 percent from 6.99 percent at Tuesday's close. The bond's yield was at 7.02 percent on Monday.

The policy-making Federal Open Market Committee voted Tuesday to hold interest rates steady, surprising stock traders, who had priced in an increase of at least one-quarter percentage point in the key federal funds rate, the rate banks charge each other for overnight loans.

The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite index rose 9.39 points to 1,224.66 in a rally fuelled by 3Com Corp.'s unexpectedly strong quarterly earnings. 3Com, a computer networking company, jumped eight to 64-5/8.
Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. said the market also focused on earnings.

"Defensive industry groups are performing better than economically sensitive, aside from technology," he said. "On the plus side we have banks, food stocks and household products -- those whose earnings tend to do well if the economy slows. On the negative side, autos and retailers."
Citicorp edged up 1/8 to 89-7/8, Sara Lee added 7/8 to 34-3/4, General Motors lost 7/8 to 47-1/2 and Sears Roebuck fell 1/4 to 45-1/2.
Wall Street again punished companies that warned that their earnings would disappoint.
Apple South slumped 7-7/8 to 13 and Checkpoint tumbled nine to 27-3/8 after both said their earnings would fall short of expectations.
"There is a deep concern that earnings are going to slow and you need to pick the stocks of companies that will continue to post good earnings," Johnson said.

Among other stocks, Loral Space rose 2-1/2 to 15-3/4 after agreeing to buy AT&T's SkyNet Satellite Services for $712.5 million. The deal would create one of the world's largest satellite-based businesses. AT&T rose 1/4 to 51-3/4 after Tuesday's 5-5/8-point drubbing on its downbeat earnings forecast.
Apria Healthcare lost 3-3/8 to 17-3/8. The company said its third-quarter income would fall short of Wall Street expectations.

TCSI Corp., a maker of communications software for telephone companies, lost 5-1/4 to 15-1/2 on market talk that the company would not meet third-quarter earnings expectations. Company officials were not available for comment.

Biotechs rallied from a summer slump after some positive industry news. Protein Design jumped 9-7/8 to 26 after the company and Roche Holding said their Zenepax drug was successful for preventing kidney transplant rejection in a late-stage trial.
Several initial public offerings drew buying interest. Snyder Communications, which provides outsourced marketing services, surged 3-5/8 to 20-5/8.
American Residential Services, a provider of heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems service, rose three to 18 and Coffee People lost 3/4 to 8-1/4.
Among stronger technology stocks, International Business Machines rose 2-3/8 to 126-1/2, Micron rose 1-1/8 to 32-1/2, Cisco Systems was up 2-11/16 to 63-3/16 and Intel added 3/4 to 97-1/4.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 0.22 of a point to 685.83. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.49 to 565.89.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.07 to 365.30. The average share was up 1 cent.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,734.858 up 11.372 or 1.17 percent.
